articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Will 'Easily Take Over 100 Hours' for Completionists to Beat, Director Teases
articles.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi teased that completionist playthroughs for the remake trilogy's conclusion could "easily take over a hundred hours" to beat.
body: The developer helping lead the charge on Cloud and the rest of the party's final assault against Sephiroth opened up about the size of the final chapter during an interview with GameSpot. We already suspected there would be a lot to do when Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC and consoles next year, but it sounds like those looking to see all Square Enix has to offer will be especially busy.

"In a standard playthrough from beginning to end, if I were to review and check every single asset and element in the game, it’ll easily take over a hundred hours," Hamaguchi said of his own playthroughs. "Obviously, I can't do that in each and every single playthrough. As the director, I don’t have enough time for that, so sometimes I would just skip combat and focus on checking the main story."

That's a lot of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation playtime. The two previous entries in the trilogy – Remake and Rebirth – proved to be large games in their own right, but the 2027 RPG finale will no doubt up the ante yet again. As Cloud, Tifa, Barret, Vincent Valentine, and the rest of the crew try to finish the fight against Sephiroth, players will use a giant airship known as the Highwind to travel.

articles.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Defies Expectations With $108 Million Box Office Opening Weekend
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil has pushed through the backlash to collect an estimated $108.3 million globally in its opening weekend at the box office. It's a franchise-best opening for the horror-comedy hybrid that saw it bring in $60 million domestically and $48.3 million internationally.
body: Starring Austin Abrams as an original character named Bryan who is thrust into the darkest pits of a suffering Raccoon City, Resident Evil's opening performance also secures its place as Cregger's biggest debut yet. His work on Barbarian earned $10 million in its opening weekend, while last year's Weapons pulled in a still-impressive $70 million. The film also features appearances from Zach Cherry (Severance), Kali Reis (True Detective: Night Country), and Paul Walter Hauser (The Fantastic Four: First Steps).

There are a few things contributing to Sony, Cregger, and Resident Evil's success in theaters. While the Abrams-led flick aimed to deliver a story inspired by survival horror gameplay, the previous run of films starring Milla Jovovich typically strayed from including the elements gamers love about the IP.

articles.title: This 40-Year-Old Video Game Is Somehow More Fun Than Ever
articles.summary: There’s something about Mario Bros. When people mention Mario today, they usually have his “super” adventures in mind, courtesy of 1985’s Super Mario Bros. But before he started knocking around turtles and other nasties in a fantasy kingdom, he was doing those same things in a backroom as he dealt…
body: Nintendo first released Mario Bros. in arcades in July 1983. It finally gave a name to the character introduced in Donkey Kong, but more importantly, it gave him a sibling. That simple addition enabled the developers to provide two-player action, essentially doubling the money an arcade machine could collect from crowds. Luigi owes a great deal to capitalism.

Gameplay resembles a 1982 arcade classic, Joust. Mario and Luigi run and jump around platforms, which wouldn’t provide much reason for concern under normal circumstances. The characters are able to fall long distances, after all, especially compared to Mario’s previous outing. However, brushing against the critters that come out of the pipes costs either plumber a life, unless the enemy has first been bopped from beneath and is temporarily stunned.

articles.title: Poppy Playtime Spinoff Escape from Playtime Gets Early Access Release Date
articles.summary: Escape from Playtime, the co-op survival horror extraction spinoff of the popular Poppy's Playtime episodic horror games that was announced at Gamescom last month, will be launching into Steam Early Access on October 21.
body: In this multiplayer spinoff, you and your friends play as Smiling Critters trapped in the abandoned Playtime Co. factory, trying to escape. You'll work together with your friends, heeding the instructions of a mysterious voice in the factory to build "a promised home for toys who prove their loyalty and usefulness." Puzzle-solving, hiding, sneaking, and careful use of communication – Escape from Playtime uses proximity chat, so if you're too loud, the Playtime Co. rejects roaming the factory will find you and destroy you.

The Poppy Playtime game franchise looks to follow in the footsteps of Five Nights at Freddy's and extend its reach into film, as developer Mob Entertainment signed a deal with Legendary Pictures in 2024 to develop a movie based on the games. There's already a line of action figures courtesy of McFarlane Toys.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

articles.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Hits Harder Than Ever
articles.summary: There are certain lines of dialogue that become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context because the words have long since transcended their…
body: Star Trek: The Original Series has plenty of those. Spock’s wish that everyone to “live long and prosper” is arguably the franchise's signature phrase. He also turned the simple word “fascinating” into a catchphrase simply by raising one eyebrow before saying it. Dr. McCoy (DeForest Kelley) spent three seasons reminding everyone, “I'm a doctor, not a…” and, at least in our collective memory declaring, “He's dead, Jim” while standing over the latest redshirt who wandered a little too far from the landing party.

On the surface, it doesn't seem like an obvious choice. It's not printed on T-shirts nearly as often as “live long and prosper.” It isn't endlessly quoted by people who have never watched an episode of Star Trek. And unlike “beam me up, Scotty,” it never became part of the broader pop culture vocabulary. But that's exactly why it's the best quote. It doesn't just capture Kirk. It captures the entire philosophy of Star Trek.
points: There are certain lines of dialogue that become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them.
Star Trek: The Original Series has plenty of those.
Spock’s wish that everyone to “live long and prosper” is arguably the franchise's signature phrase.

articles.title: Fire Emblem Is Officially Nintendo’s Strongest GOTY 2026 Contender
articles.summary: I don't think I had "Fire Emblem gets a Game of the Year nomination at The Game Awards" on my bingo card for 2026 — or for any other year, for that matter. But I think it's a possibility. In fact, I think it's almost definitely going to happen. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is a contender.
body: That doesn't mean it's going to win. It increasingly looks like nothing will come even close to getting in Grand Theft Auto 6 's way. But it does mean that, in a weak field, Nintendo and developer Intelligent Systems have muscled their way to the front of the pack through sheer force of conviction.

Fire Emblem would once have been considered far too niche to attract Game of the Year attention from The Game Awards jury. It's an RPG, sure — one of the jurors' favored genres. But it's also a tactics RPG. It's basically a strategy game, and no strategy game has ever secured a GOTY nomination.

Things started to change for Intelligent Systems' series in the 2010s, though. First, there was Fire Emblem Awakening for the 3DS, which is still widely considered the best entry in the series. It attracted enough critical acclaim to start to break through with players who weren't particular fans of the genre. Gaming's cognoscenti took notice.

articles.title: Call of Duty maker Activision claims video game cheating is now a £6.3 billion ($8.5 billion) a year industry
articles.summary: Activision has published a breakdown of the numbers behind cheating in its games, claiming cheating is big business, generating about £6.3 billion - $8.5bn - every year in account sales, boosting, and spoofing services.
body: In a blog posted on the publisher's website, the publisher's cheat squad, Team Ricochet, said cheat subscriptions across 15 games alone generate around £2.6 billion ($3.5 billion).

Activision said it has "paired technical detection with sustained legal action to destabilise the cheat ecosystem at every level", disrupting more than 375 reseller operations, issuing more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and shutting down 31 primary cheat vendors.

The publisher also claims cheat sellers regularly hide the fact their products have been detected, instead blaming outages on excuses like illness, surgery or car accidents to keep customers on side before admitting their cheats are no longer working.

Activision says the crackdown is also driving up costs for cheaters themselves, with subscriptions costing upwards of £75 ($100), spoofing tools adding further recurring fees, and some players spending more than £750 ($1,000) a year in total.

articles.title: Ace Attorney Trilogy Passed An Impressive Milestone, But No New Game Is In Sight
articles.summary: To celebrate the franchise's impending 25th anniversary on Oct. 12, Capcom announced that Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy reached a new sales milestone. Sadly, we still don't know if another Ace Attorney game will be released, or if a new one is even in development right now.
body: On Bluesky, Capcom shared that Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy, a collection released for modern consoles in 2019, has sold over 5 million copies. According to data on Capcom's investor relations website, the franchise as a whole has sold over 15 million copies. New artwork by Kazuya Nuri and Takuro Fuse was also shared to mark the sales milestone and celebrate the franchise's quarter-century anniversary.

Although that Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy sales milestone might seem quaint when compared to Capcom giants like Monster Hunter: World or Resident Evil 2's remake, it's still a respectable feat for a collection of courtroom visual novels that could be considered quite niche. Ace Attorney has a hardcore, passionate community, and Capcom has served them in recent years with re-releases of almost every game in the series.

articles.title: First 5-day Tokyo Game Show in 30 years cuts back to 4 in face of Typhoon Dujuan
articles.summary: As reported by Kotaku, the organizers of the Tokyo Game Show have announced that its final day has been canceled and tickets for Monday, September 21 will be refunded.
body: "Due to the approach of Typhoon No. 25, strong winds and rain are expected to intensify in the afternoon and beyond, and disruptions to transportation are also a concern," event organizers wrote on Twitter. "Therefore, prioritizing the safety of all attendees, exhibitors, and related parties, as well as ensuring safe return home, we have decided to cancel the event for the entire day."
The TGS showfloor will remain open for today, September 20, with potential modifications. There is no word on how the event will address publishers and devs who rented out space for the final day.

As reported by the Japan Times, Dujuan is the 25th named typhoon of 2026, and is predicted to dump the heaviest rainfall (almost 16 inches) on the Kanto region containing Tokyo. Nippon Airways has canceled many flights in the region, while the East Japan Railway is fully and partially suspending service on some lines.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima responds to accusations of Physint being over budget and late on deadline, says he still "loves Sony" despite collapse of publishing deal
articles.summary: Last week, we learned that Sony "stepped away" from Kojima Production's previously PlayStation-exclusive "action espionage" game Physint. Following the announcement, which saw Xbox take over publishing duties for the in-development title, a new report has claimed Sony's decision was the result of…
body: Now, IGN has conducted an interview with Kojima that sheds a little more light on the situation. In the chat - which covers a range of topics including Kojima's fears for the future of the studio, the perils of working on multiple projects at once, and the implications of losing Sony resources - Kojima detailed how the conversation with the platform holder went, noting how that he was in a state of shock at the time, and finds the meeting difficult to recall.

"I don't remember so much of that meeting, to be honest with you," Kojima told IGN. "And my colleagues probably don't remember as well, so I can't really answer if you ask me what exactly they said. But, from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry.

"Nothing could've prepared me for their decision to step away from the project. So I thought, "What am I going to do from tomorrow?" But from my side, I love Sony. And I don't have any bad feelings against them because I know that it's a tough time in the game industry."

articles.title: Elden Ring Nightreign is dead, but modders are dabbing on its corpse, with one porting an entire Dark Souls 2 DLC zone as a playable map
articles.summary: Modder Doneda has released a particularly funky and exciting mod for elden Ring Nightreign, porting Dark Souls 2's Frozen Eleum Loyce and Frigid Outskirts as a standalone map. They also have a trailer up for the project on YouTube.
body: Gun to my head, I think the Brume Tower is my favorite DS2 level, but Eleum Loyce still feels like a dear old friend. I enjoyed base DS2 more than most, but the Lost Crowns DLCs were on a whole different level. Other FromSoft DLCs may be better in a vacuum (Old Hunters, Shadow of the Erdtree), but there has never been a more staggering, exhilarating leap in quality between one of the studio's games and its corresponding expansion.

While Brume Tower may be my beautiful baby, it just wouldn't fit in Nightreign like Eleum Loyce does: The wide open Outskirts and walled city can mimic the mini open world of Limveld in a way the twisty, narrow Brume Tower couldn't manage. My favorite detail is that it looks like the night two circle narrows down on the underground chaos arena where you fight the Burnt Ivory King, a fun and creative recontextualizing of the level's original flow.

Doneda's new map is already available for download on the Nightreign Nexus. You'll need to install Mod Engine 3 beforehand to run it⁠—most, if not all Nightreign mods require the utility. Doneda seems intent on making more modded Nightreign maps, and you can follow their work on YouTube or support them via Ko-fi.

articles.title: Take to the skies and shoot your mates in the face with a shotgun in Fish & Ships
articles.summary: Perhaps the most famous British meal is fish and chips. It's hard to beat a perfectly battered, crispy piece of fish, served with salty, pillowy soft chips absolutely drowned in vinegar. I'm getting hungry just thinking about it.
body: If you enjoy co-op games like Peak, then Fish & Ships looks like it'll be right up your alley. Take to the skies with your mates and engage in some shenanigans.

It looks like you've got to navigate your craft through a ravine with multiple plateaus cut into the cliff faces where hilarity can ensue, like shooting an old guy in the face with a shotgun. Damn, he was just sitting on his porch enjoying the sunshine. Let's assume he was guarding something necessary to progress, shall we?

As well as guns, the fish have a lot of boxes (maybe those contain the guns?) that you can throw overboard and smash into each other's faces. Physical comedy is a big selling point of Fish & Ships. There's also a shot of the airship trying to navigate a floating minefield, it looks tricky.

I can see this game being incredibly fun to watch streamers play. I, unfortunately, do not have a big enough group of PC pals to pull off the kind of aerial hijinks seen in the trailer, but I'd love to see other people taking part in all the fun.

articles.title: Feel like a kid again when toy car game Obstacle Overdrive launches October 2
articles.summary: If you were fortunate enough to have toy cars when you were a kid—or rad enough to buy them for yourself as an adult—you probably had fun driving them over absolutely everything in your room. Mine could climb walls, scramble over book mountains, and drift around VHS-case race tracks.
body: Developed and published by Arcane Ermine, Obstacle Overdrive lets you go off-road—because it's all in a '90s bedroom—and make miniature radio-controlled cars navigate wacky obstacle courses. In the trailer, we see trucks going over toy keyboards, shimmying around block boards, and trundling over mountains of soft plushy toys.

Relive childhood memories and navigate your radio controlled cars over obstacle courses built out of toys in Obstacle Overdrive. The game launches October 2 and you can wishlist it and download the demo on Steam.

It's important to note this isn't a racing game. There are no other people to compete with, it's just you and the track, so take your time and learn how to overcome each area. You can also use five different cars, all with their own feel, so try them all out and see which handles each course best.

You can even collect hats that the cars can wear, which is just adorable. You may have to go even further off the beaten track than normal to get at them, but it'll all be worth it when you see how sweet they look.

videos.title: Cairn - On the Trail DLC Launch Date Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Start the climb of a lifetime:
body: On the Trail is a series of free DLCs for the award winning survival climbing game Cairn. Set out on the ascent of a lifetime with pro-climber Aava: climb anywhere, plan your route carefully, and manage your resources to survive the unforgiving ascent of Mount Kami.

On the Trail brings climbers to new climbing spots and challenges. Find your route freely, solve fresh climbing problems and explore new iconic locations as you follow the trail of a legendary climber.

Cairn features realistic simulation that allows you to climb intuitively, anywhere. Find the best holds and place your hands and feet seamlessly with simple controls. Adapt your posture, effort and balance - if you're not careful, you will fall!
points: On the Trail is a series of free DLCs for the award winning survival climbing game Cairn.
